subject: Joan Wallach Scott, not James C. Scott

proposals.relationship: Scott argues that Stone’s unequal standards marginalize women’s history and exclude it from defining standards for historical scholarship (1985).
proposals.evidence_note: Scott concedes that his treatment of the two books was generally fair; her criticism concerns his framing and unequal criteria.
primary_locators: NYRB letter, paragraphs beginning “In its detail” and “The asymmetry,” through final paragraph

proposals.relationship: Replying to Scott, Stone defends reciprocal standards for studying men and women together while apologizing for the tone of his commandments (1985).
proposals.evidence_note: A substantive disagreement within the same exchange, not a second controversy or a denial of Stone’s apology.
primary_locators: “Lawrence Stone replies,” all four response paragraphs after his opening explanation

proposals.relationship: Scott rejects Palmer’s opposition between discourse and class struggle, arguing that class and gender must be analyzed together rather than chosen as competing priorities (1987).
proposals.evidence_note: Discourse includes institutions and social practices, not words alone. This adds the missing reply direction to the exchange already described in edge_920; it is not a newly discovered second debate. Palmer’s own article was not freshly reread.
primary_locators: A Reply to Criticism, printed pp.39–43, especially40; concluding45

proposals.relationship: Scott argues that Thompson’s use of experience makes class identity foundational and obscures the contested construction of gender and other differences (1991).
proposals.evidence_note: She praises his transformative history while disputing its conceptual foundation. Note24 acknowledges Sewell’s different reading. This is Scott’s interpretation, not consensus; Thompson’s books remain unread here. Distinct from the mixed Ranter exchange in edge_511.
primary_locators: The Evidence of Experience, printed pp.784–786, including n.24
